race_context: The district: Southwest Allen County Schools (SACS, officially MSD of Southwest Allen County Schools) serves the southwest Fort Wayne area of Allen County {sacs_leadership}{idoe_enroll}. It runs six elementary schools (Aboite, Covington, Deer Ridge, Haverhill, Lafayette Meadows and Whispering Meadows), two middle schools (Summit and Woodside), Homestead High School and the online school eSACS {sacs_leadership}{jg_policy_vote}. State data show 7,389 students in 2026, down from 7,853 in 2023 {idoe_enroll}. In September 2026 the district estimated fall enrollment at 7,286, up 30 students from the year before {jg_budget2026}.

Superintendent: Dr. Joshua D. St. John {sacs_leadership}. He was previously Summit Middle School's principal and became assistant superintendent of secondary education in July 2023, under then-Superintendent Park Ginder {jg_officers2023}.

Board: five members, each serving a four-year term {sacs_board}{jg_preview2022}. Doug Copley (president) and the two incumbents on this ballot, Kimberly Moppert (vice president) and Stephanie Veit (secretary), hold at-large seats. Bradley Mills holds the Aboite Township seat and Mark Gilpin, a member since 2000, holds the Lafayette Township seat {sacs_board}. State 2024 results use different labels for the seats Copley and Mills won ('District 1' for Copley and 'At Large' for Mills), which does not match the district's list {enr_2024}{sacs_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows 'vote for 1' {in_list}. But the district lists both Moppert's and Veit's at-large terms as ending December 31, 2026, and they won those seats together in 2022, when state results show two seats {sacs_board}{enr_2022}. The Journal Gazette reported that two SACS seats are on the 2026 ballot {jg_filing0612}. So this race elects TWO members, and the two candidates on the ballot would fill both seats.

Who is running: both incumbents filed as Republicans and no one filed against them. The Journal Gazette reported SACS was the only Allen County district with no contested school board race {jg_filing0618}{jg_filing0612}. 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could declare a party; the seats were previously nonpartisan {jg_filing0612}.

Budget (September 2026): the proposed 2027 budget is $120 million: $61 million for the education fund, $26 million for operations, $25.6 million for debt service and $7.8 million from the operating referendum. A hearing was set for September 15 and adoption for October 6 {jg_budget2026}. Voters renewed the operating referendum in 2022 {jg_budget2026}{jg_preview2022}. It pays salaries and benefits for 80 employees, including 67 teachers and 11 counselors, and for five school resource officers {jg_budget2026}.

SEA 1 (July 2025): Chief Operating Officer Randi Libby told the board the district had planned for the expected budget effects of the 2025 property-tax law. She said: 'We're going to have less revenue, that's not an option, there's going to be less revenue across the state.' The district said it would know more once net assessed values were released on August 1 {wane_sea1}.

Enrollment and open enrollment: officials said SACS lost more than 500 students after enrollment peaked at nearly 7,800 in fall 2021, and 2025-26 was the fourth year in a row of decline {jg_policy_vote}. On October 21, 2025, the board approved policy changes allowing limited enrollment of non-resident students and more in-district transfers, to fill open seats in existing classrooms {jg_policy_vote}{jg_transfers2026}. In August 2026 the board approved 180 non-resident transfers for 2026-27. The superintendent said 26 applications were denied, for reasons including lack of space and the policy's behavior and attendance rules {jg_transfers2026}.
Facilities: in October 2025 the board hired the Hagerman Group as construction manager for a planned $32 million career center on land directly west of Covington Elementary School {jg_policy_vote}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum or questionnaire for this race, which is uncontested.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, first elected in 2022 and listed as a Republican; a retired SACS teacher {sacs_board}{enr_2022}{jg_officers2023}{in_list}.
background: A SACS graduate who taught in the district for 20 years. She co-founded Mr. McGregor's Garden, a children's book and toy store in the Village at Coventry that has since closed {jg_preview2022}.
Described as a retired district teacher when she joined the board in January 2023 {jg_officers2023}.
Board vice president, serving since January 2023 {sacs_board}.
path_to_ballot: Won an at-large seat in 2022 as the top vote-getter (7,836 votes) in a five-candidate race for two seats {enr_2022}{jg_officers2023}.
Filed for re-election as a Republican and is unopposed {jg_filing0612}{jg_filing0618}{in_list}.

items: In 2022 she said the board needed a member with classroom experience: 'It's time that we really had someone (on the board) who knows what it's like to be a teacher, knows the highs and lows of those kinds of things.' She also said, 'You can't micromanage all the time what's going on in the classroom' {jg_preview2022}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and vice president {sacs_board}. When she took office in January 2023 she said, 'I'm going to do my best to do what's best for kids' {jg_officers2023}. This guide found no 2026 statement from her on the board's record.
plans: In 2022 she said she would be guided by what is best for students {jg_preview2022}. No 2026 campaign plans found.
endorsements_finance: In 2022 campaign finance filings showed she received $8,000 from the Indiana Political Action Committee for Education, the political arm of the Indiana State Teachers Association {jg_preview2022}.

In October 2022 she was one of several school board candidates who introduced themselves at an Allen County Republican Party fundraiser. The party chairman said the appearances were not party endorsements {jg_morris2022}.
No 2026 endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

Her individual votes and statements on the 2025 enrollment policy, the budget and the career center were not found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board secretary, first elected in 2022 and listed as a Republican {sacs_board}{enr_2022}{in_list}.
background: In 2022 she was director of airport development at the Fort Wayne-Allen County Airport Authority. She was previously business development manager at The Hagerman Group and a commercial lender at 3Rivers Federal Credit Union {jg_preview2022}.
She has said she does not have a background in education but has experience in construction and master planning {jg_preview2022}.
path_to_ballot: Won an at-large seat in 2022 with 6,644 votes, finishing just ahead of then-incumbent Doug Copley (6,635) in a five-candidate race for two seats. A December 2022 recount confirmed her win {enr_2022}{jg_officers2023}.
Filed for re-election as a Republican and is unopposed {jg_filing0612}{jg_filing0618}{in_list}.

items: In 2022 she said her construction and master-planning experience would help SACS manage enrollment growth and student capacity at its elementary and middle schools {jg_preview2022}.

In October 2025, when the board discussed the non-resident transfer policy, she explained that the salary thresholds for giving priority to non-resident employees' children are meant to favor full-time staff over, for example, someone who coached one season or substitute taught twice {jg_policy_draft}.
In 2022 she said she would use her private-sector experience to engage the community in the schools' work {jg_preview2022}.
At the September 2026 budget presentation she said the board gets asked a lot what the referendum pays for, and said she appreciated the information {jg_budget2026}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member and secretary {sacs_board}. This guide found no 2026 campaign statement from her on the board's record.
endorsements_finance: In 2022 campaign finance filings showed $1,000 from the Indiana Political Action Committee for Education (the Indiana State Teachers Association's political arm) and $500 from Therese Brown, then a Republican candidate for Allen County commissioner {jg_preview2022}.

In October 2022 she was one of several school board candidates who introduced themselves at an Allen County Republican Party fundraiser. The party chairman said the appearances were not party endorsements {jg_morris2022}.
